question: When TemporalAssemblyMemory reaches max_candidates with only mature stale candidates, does the current prune policy deny a genuinely dissimilar new pattern indefinitely, while an otherwise matched immature stale candidate is reclaimable?
reduction_question: If mature saturation blocks acquisition, is the effect fully explained by the bounded max_candidates resource policy plus prune eligibility restricted to low-episode immature candidates rather than an additional memory mechanism?

implementation_experiment.head: 3cac844ca6a80725c87d7e681c23b703f35150c2
arms: MATURE_SATURATED: mature P1 and P2, then P3 at 100ms and 1000ms
IMMATURE_RECLAIMABLE: mature P1, observe P2 once, then P3 at 100ms

observations.mechanistic_reduction: At capacity, observe() invokes prune(); prune() only removes stale candidates whose episode_count is <= immature_stale_episodes. Mature candidates are therefore outside this reclamation path, so a dissimilar new pattern cannot acquire a slot once all slots are mature under the fixed probe.
observations.default_structural_relation: Default mature_episodes=3 and immature_stale_episodes=2 preserve the same mature-outside-prune relation, but this synthetic cap-two probe does not establish that supported/default workloads saturate max_candidates=256.
observations.interpretation: Architecture/resource and lifelong-plasticity semantics concern; not scientific evidence or mechanistic novelty.

what_would_falsify_or_reduce_it: Reduce to REJECT/ENGINEERING_NOTE_ONLY if the supported contract explicitly defines permanent mature retention as a hard lifetime capacity with no ongoing acquisition requirement, if supported workloads cannot plausibly approach mature saturation, or if a fresh resource-matched identity-neutral turnover comparator produces no difference on a prospectively fixed downstream learnability observable.
